title: Product discovery, reviews and apps
summary: Help customers find, understand and trust a product before choosing tools.
why: Filters, comparisons and credible reviews reduce buying effort, especially for complex or expensive products.
Every app adds cost, scripts and data responsibilities. Check native features first.
know: Search & Discovery manages search, filters and recommendations. A headless storefront needs the corresponding Storefront API implementation.
Review tools such as Judge.me collect, moderate and display reviews. XTERRA has an integration; that does not make it mandatory for every store.
Use verified specifications for comparisons and quizzes. Never invent compatibility or benefits.
Assess bundles, upsells and subscriptions against margin, stock and demand. Durable goods may not suit recurring subscriptions.
Record the purpose, native alternative, headless support, cost, permissions, export and removal options for each app.
inputs: Product specifications, categories, search terms, zero-result queries, support questions and funnel data
Installed apps, storefront architecture, budget and rights to review data
actions: Separate essentials from options. Fix product fields, prices and out-of-stock rules first.
Test filters, synonyms, comparisons and recommendations against product, accessory and variant relationships.
Preserve review provenance and status during migration; verify counts, averages and privacy. Do not manufacture reviews.
Test representative and empty searches, stockouts, mobile and keyboard use. Check APIs, webhooks and performance.
done: Customers can find purchasable products; recommended prices and stock match the cart.
Reviews are traceable and deduplicated. App choices have reasons.
pitfalls: Expecting a theme widget to appear on an Astro frontend.
Hard-coding review averages or recommendations that later become stale.
decision: Agree on the buying journey, app costs and whether the improvement justifies maintenance.

reader.concept: Search, filters, comparisons, recommendations and reviews answer different questions during product selection.
reader.when: Use this when products are hard to compare or customers need more confidence to buy.

example.situation: A shopper wants foldable equipment, but the only filter is brand.
example.lesson: Build filters around real buying criteria.

reader.first_step: List three common buying questions and the functions that answer them.
